top_choice_rationale: Kane, Mele and Molenkamp is the point where a sharp theoretical prediction (a bulk Z2 invariant forcing protected edge states) met a clean device in HgTe wells in 2007 and survived, and it has been confirmed by transport, ARPES and STM in independent laboratories for fifteen to twenty years. The allocation keeps the founding Kane-Mele pair together and the citation can be limited to the quantum spin Hall effect and protected edge states, which separates it from the 2016 topological-phases prize. The cost is that 3D topological insulators, Hasan, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Fu-Moore-Balents are left outside. Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a mature, well-reproduced and clean two-name prize, but distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a closer judgement and lies outside my field. An award is better than no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as WACQT director and a Chalmers superconducting-circuits theorist I have no direct tie to topological insulators or lattice clocks, though the profile does flag possible general conflict-of-interest in quantum technology
